purpose: Provider-aligned routing contract for Palantir Foundry, Ontology, AIP, Gotham, Defense OSDK, Automate, Apollo and JupyterLab Code Workspaces across the XUNIA / ZYRA ecosystem.

Foundry.role: governed ingestion, transforms, datasets, lineage and application data substrate

AIP.role: agent reasoning, LLM workflows, automations and evals

Ontology.role: objects, links, properties, actions, functions and operational state

Gotham.role: authorized defense/intelligence operational workflows over dynamic ontology data

Defense OSDK.role: typed defense application SDK contract for intelligence, mission planning, order of battle and sustainment

Automate.role: event/time-driven effects using Ontology Actions and AIP Logic

JupyterLab.role: Foundry Code Workspace for analysis, models, notebooks and Ontology interaction
requires: AIP enabled for AIP coding agent

routing_policy: Use Foundry for governed ingestion, transforms, lineage and application data.
Use AIP for model-assisted reasoning and agent workflows.
Use the Ontology as the governed operational source of truth rather than unmanaged agent memory.
Use Gotham only for data and workflows exposed to the authorized Gotham enrollment.
Use Defense OSDK only through tenant-generated typed clients and the invoking identity's permissions.
Do not expose autonomous local targeting-and-fires execution; represent such data only where authorized for read-only context, simulation or review.
Use Automate for bounded event/time workflows; stage consequential effects for human review where policy requires.
Use Apollo for governed software delivery, never as ambient remote execution authority.
Use JupyterLab Code Workspaces for exploratory analysis, model development and notebook-based Ontology work.
Re-authorize every cross-plane action and preserve identity, markings, provenance and audit logs.
truthfulness_rule: Configuration flags describe intended integration only. They never imply Palantir licensing, enrollment, entitlement, credentials, connectivity, government affiliation, mission authority or weapons-release authority.

terminology.jupiter: Normalized to JupyterLab because current Palantir documentation exposes JupyterLab through Code Workspaces; no Palantir product named Jupiter was verified.
